title: Cooking Without Recipes

learn.summary: The endgame is template thinking: a stir-fry, a frittata, a grain bowl, a braise, and a pan sauce are not recipes but frameworks with swappable parts. You already hold the levers — salt, fat, acid, heat, umami, and a thermometer — so the fridge becomes a puzzle instead of a dead end. Recipes become sheet music you can sight-read, depart from, and return to.

do: Cook one dinner this week with zero recipes: open the fridge, pick a protein, vegetable, and starch, and build the plate using only technique

children.title: Meal Templates

learn.summary: Learn five templates and you can cook for a lifetime: stir-fry (protein + vegetable + aromatics + sauce over rice), frittata (eggs + anything + cheese), grain bowl (grain + roasted vegetable + protein + dressing + crunch), pasta (pasta + fat + vegetable or protein + starchy water + cheese), and sheet-pan dinner (protein + vegetables + 425°F). Each is a fill-in-the-blank, not a formula to memorize. Write your five on a card and iterate weekly.

do: Pick one template — stir-fry or sheet-pan — and cook it twice this week with completely different fillings, keeping the structure identical

children.title: Meal Planning

learn.summary: Planning is not rigid menus; it is one 20-minute Sunday session: pick 3-4 dinners, shop once, and prep the bottlenecks — wash greens, cook a pot of grains, make a jar of vinaigrette, maybe roast a tray of vegetables. Plan ingredients that cascade: a roast chicken becomes tacos becomes stock. Cooks who plan eat better and cheaper on the same effort.

do: This Sunday, spend 20 minutes planning 3 dinners around one cascading ingredient, write one shopping list, and prep one component ahead

children.title: Loving Leftovers

learn.summary: Leftovers are pre-cooked ingredients, not punishments: yesterday's rice is tomorrow's fried rice (day-old rice fries better than fresh), roast vegetables become frittatas and grain bowls, braised meat becomes tacos and sandwiches. Reheat to 165°F, use refrigerated leftovers within 3-4 days, and freeze anything you will not reach in time. A weekly fridge-clearing meal — call it a hash, a soup, or a frittata — is the highest form of the skill.

do: Declare one fridge-clearing dinner this week and transform at least two leftovers into a genuinely new dish — fried rice, frittata, or soup
